blocks.text: Erythroblastosis foetalis is a haemolytic disease of the foetus or newborn caused by Rh incompatibility between an Rh-negative pregnant mother and an Rh-positive foetus.

It occurs when an Rh-negative mother (dd) carries an Rh-positive baby (DD or Dd). Foetal blood may enter the mother's blood; exposed to the foetal Rh antigens, she makes anti-Rh antibodies. These cross the placenta into the foetal blood and destroy the foetal red cells, causing haemolytic anaemia and other serious complications.

blocks.alt: Top: a section of the placenta. The umbilical cord with its blood vessels joins the chorion; branched chorionic villi carrying foetal vessels hang into the maternal blood pool, which is fed by maternal arteries and veins from the uterine wall. A small square in the blood pool is enlarged below. Bottom left: foetal red cells pass out of a villus into the mother's blood, where her B cells make anti-Rh antibodies. Bottom right: maternal anti-Rh antibodies enter the villi and the foetal blood.

items: In severe cases the destruction of foetal red cells can cause miscarriage or stillbirth.
If the foetus survives, its liver and spleen enlarge as they try to make more red cells.
Breakdown of red cells produces bilirubin, which builds up and causes jaundice (yellow skin and eyes); high bilirubin can also damage brain cells.
The surviving baby's blood is replaced with Rh-negative blood free of anti-Rh antibodies.

blocks.title: Tidbit: prevention with anti-Rh serum
blocks.text: When Rh incompatibility is possible, the mother is given an injection of Rh antiserum (serum containing anti-Rh antibodies) in early pregnancy and immediately after birth. It destroys any of the baby's red cells that have crossed into her blood before they can sensitise her immune system.

blocks.title: Tidbit: ABO incompatibility can protect
blocks.text: If an O-negative mother carries an A-positive or B-positive baby, any foetal red cells entering her blood are quickly destroyed by her existing anti-A or anti-B antibodies, before she can form anti-Rh antibodies.
